name: Ranim
role: Rust scenes rendered headless through wgpu and FFmpeg to MP4, PNG frames and timed captures
summary: Manim-style animation engine in Rust. A scene is a function that inserts vector items and plays animations on a timeline. Rendering writes MP4, WebM or MOV with alpha, GIF, saved PNG frames, and PNG captures at marked times, using wgpu. Pre-1.0 with unstable APIs; the first build compiles a large dependency tree.
use_when: Compiled, GPU-rendered maths-style vector motion authored in Rust
Over Manim Community when Rust and render speed matter
Fixed-time PNG captures from a scene to inspect frames
avoid_when: Equations and LaTeX explainers: Manim Community
A stable API is needed: pre-1.0 releases break often

install.macos: cargo add ranim --features render (FFmpeg on PATH)

notes: 2026-11-27: Lead matched: 0.2.1, MIT. README targets an unreleased v0.3 API. The render entry point needs the `render` feature. Without ffmpeg on PATH it downloads one into the working directory.

evidence.result: Headless wgpu render of a 1 s 320x180 12 fps scene gave 12 PNG frames, an h264 MP4 with 12 frames and 3 time-mark captures. Square bbox 46 to 64 px (45 degree turn). Captures equalled frames 0, 6 and 11; second run was byte-identical.
evidence.scope: Ranim 0.2.1 library route, Rust 1.95.0, macOS arm64 Apple GPU, one rotating square. Same-machine repeat only; no CLI, preview, text, alpha or other GPUs.

assessment.rationale: 0.2.1 on crates.io, MIT, last push 2026-11-17. Library API renders offline through wgpu and FFmpeg. Compiled alternative to Manim Community and Motion Canvas. Pre-1.0 and API-unstable.
